profile.designer: Combat Vehicles Research and Development Establishment (CVRDE)

through_line: The design idea of a third-generation main battle tank with a focus on indigenous development and technological advancements has survived every revision of the Arjun tank.

stages.title: Initial Conceptualization
stages.summary: The Indian Ministry of Defence initiated the development of a new main battle tank to elevate its armored corps, with the Combat Vehicles Research and Development Establishment (CVRDE) leading the project. The initial plan was to develop a tank with a 105mm gun.
stages.driver: Need for a modern main battle tank
stages.impact: Marked the beginning of India's indigenous tank development program

stages.title: First Prototype Development
stages.summary: The first prototype of the Arjun tank was rolled out, resembling the German Leopard 2A4 tank. The prototype underwent extensive trials, highlighting major issues such as engine overheating and suboptimal performance of the weapon system.
stages.impact: Led to significant delays and redesigns

stages.title: Extensive Trials and Testing
stages.summary: The Indian Army carried out extensive trials of the Arjun tank, identifying major shortcomings and leading to further design changes and improvements.
stages.driver: Need for improved performance and reliability
stages.impact: Resulted in significant improvements to the tank's design and capabilities

stages.title: Initial Operational Capability
stages.summary: The Arjun tank entered service with the Indian Army, marking a significant milestone in India's indigenous tank development program.
stages.driver: Need for a modern main battle tank

stages.title: Improved Variant Development
stages.summary: The Arjun Mk2 variant was introduced, featuring major and minor improvements to the armored vehicle's design, including a re-designed turret and improved armor.
stages.driver: Need for improved performance and capabilities

stages.title: Modernization and Upgrades
stages.summary: The Arjun Mk1A variant was introduced, featuring further improvements and upgrades, including a completely re-designed turret and improved armor protection.
stages.driver: Need for continued modernization and improvement
stages.impact: Enhanced the tank's capabilities and effectiveness

stages.title: Current Status and Future Developments
stages.summary: The Arjun tank remains in service with the Indian Army, with ongoing efforts to improve and upgrade its capabilities. The Indian Ministry of Defence has ordered 118 Mk1A battle tanks, with a focus on continued indigenous development and technological advancements.
stages.driver: Need for continued modernization and improvement
stages.impact: Will continue to enhance India's armored capabilities
